subject: Dedicated capacity recap - Vivalife Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Qureshi <aisha.qureshi@vivalifehealth.com>; Tom Reyes <treyes@vivalifehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap - Vivalife Health

Hi Aisha / Tom -

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we're all aligned and to capture next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of customer goals / pain:
- Reduce generation latency for patient-facing workflows (current p95 ~ 1.4s unacceptable for some UIs).
- Remove noisy multi-tenant interference - priority to isolation for PHI/PII use cases.
- Predictable throughput during business hours (spikes during 8am-11am PT).
- Strong SLA and auditability for security/compliance.

What we heard (desired outcomes):
- Dedicated GPU pool (reserved capacity) that is isolated from other Redwood customers.
- Capacity to handle ~600 concurrent requests during peak, average token lengths ~150-300, typical prompt mix is classification + generation.
- Target latency: p99 < 900ms for short-turn generation, p95 < 400ms for embedding calls.
- Audit logs and KMS integration for keys; retention configurable to 90 days for the initial contract.

Redwood proposed configuration (initial):
- Dedicated cluster: 8 x NVIDIA A100 80GB (reserved) with node pinning to ensure isolation; autoscale headroom of +2 nodes for burst.
- Inference profile: reduced-quantization mixed-fp16 path for latency-sensitive models; KV cache warmup and prefix caching for common prompts.
- Network isolation: customer VPC peering + private control plane (no public egress for model data).
- SLA targets: 99.9% uptime on the Dedicated cluster, latency SLOs as above with automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant if SLOs at risk.

Estimated timeline & next steps:
- Redwood to share formal capacity proposal + draft SLA (attached) by EOD Monday.
- VivaLife to confirm security questionnaire items outstanding and any additional compliance needs (Aisha).
- Schedule technical design review with your infra team - suggest Tue 2/16 or Wed 2/17 (30-45m).
- Procurement: rough cost ballpark shared in follow-up; finalize after technical design.

Attachments included: vivalife_requirements.pdf (your notes) and initial SLA draft.

Action items:
- Aisha: confirm if additional data residency constraints (EU-only) apply - I think you said US-only, please confirm.
- Tom: ok to schedule tech deep-dive Tue/Wed?
- Rishi/Dev: I'll loop you into the HubSpot deal and add technical config details.

Thanks -

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap - Vivalife Health

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. This matches our notes. A few clarifications:

1) Data residency: confirmed US-only for now; we may revisit EU later.
2) Compliance: we will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and KMS integration; I'll send a short questionnaire back.
3) Throughput: the 600 concurrent is conservative - our internal estimate is 450 med-size requests, but we'd like headroom.

Two asks before the tech deep-dive:
- Can you include a cost estimate range for the 8x A100 config vs a 6x A100 with higher autoscale headroom? We want to show both to finance.
- Can Rishi/Dev confirm whether the private control plane option supports our internal SIEM forwarding?

Tue 2/16 10:00-10:45 PT works for our infra lead; tentative accept on calendar.

Thanks -
Aisha
Aisha Qureshi
Head of Platform Engineering | VivaLife Health
aisha.qureshi@vivalifehealth.com | +1 (206) 555-0122
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Qureshi <aisha.qureshi@vivalifehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>; Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap - Vivalife Health

Thanks Marissa / Aisha - looping in a quick technical confirmation:

- Private control plane supports syslog/forwarding to customer SIEM (we have out-of-band connectors to Splunk/Datadog/Sumo); we'll add the connector in the deployment checklist.
- KMS: we support AWS KMS and external HSM via our key-wrap flow; we can validate with your security team during the tech review.
- Autoscale behavior: reserved pool of 8 nodes, autoscale threshold configured at 75% CPU/GPU utilization with a 120s evaluation window; burst +2 nodes will kick in for short spikes.
- Latency: with mixed-fp16 and prefix caching we expect p95 in the 300-450ms range for the short prompts you described; p99 < 900ms targeted subject to model choice and token sizes.

I've attached a short SLA draft with operational definitions and escalation windows - take a look and we'll refine during the review.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
